articles.title: Description of Ghosts and Stone-Throwers in Vourvoura by K. I. Mantzouranіs
articles.author: K. I. Mantzouranіs
articles.excerpt: Folkloric study on ghosts in Greek Folklore and Traditions. They appear as humans, animals or rocks; some are heard only. They are souls of the dead — Christians in human form, Turks as dogs. They appear near desolate churches and hollow trees after midnight. Where a man was slain a Chamodraki appears.

image.alt: Old church in Greek Folklore and Traditions, a site where ghosts appear

content.value: Belief in ghosts is very strong in Vourvoura. Many people told us they have seen ghosts. Ghosts are beings of many forms and usually harmless. They appear either as humans or as animals in many different forms — donkeys, goats, she-goats, dogs, cats — and at other times as inanimate objects such as rocks.
Many are seen, but only their voice is heard — usually men who were unjustly slain, making sounds such as cries and moans.
Others cause loud noises; some throw stones at people, which cause no pain or wounds.
Some are the souls of the dead — human in form if they were Christians, and in the form of dogs if they were Turks — while in others we do not know their origin.
They appear mainly near desolate churches and beside old and large trees with great hollows, as a rule at night and always after midnight.
Wherever a man has been killed, a Chamodraki appears. This is a small child in appearance, with fire in its mouth.
Ghosts are seen only by those gifted with second sight.

articles.title: Papazuras and the Invisible Net – Kastri
articles.author: K. I. Mantzouranіs
articles.excerpt: Folkloric account of Papazuras's experience at the Ladiko near Vourvoura. He encountered an invisible net blocking his way and heard chanting and voices. With exorcisms he dispelled the phenomenon, but at the chapel of Agia Paraskevi he heard wooden pitcher lids without seeing anyone.

image.alt: The desolate chapel of Agia Paraskevi near Kastri, Arcadia

content.value: Papazuras was coming from Kastri. Inside the Ladiko (east of Vourvoura), where the Platana is, a net appeared before him and would not let him pass. The worst of it was that he began to hear loud chanting and voices in front of him.

He began to recite exorcisms and the net vanished. He passed through, but as soon as he stepped inside the desolate little chapel of Agia Paraskevi, he heard the lids of wooden pitchers banging. He assumed these were women who had gone to the spring to fetch water. He looked left and right but saw no one. He left and returned home barely alive.

articles.title: The Pariorites
articles.author: Chr. V. Fragkoulis
articles.excerpt: Folkloric tale from Megali Mantineia: the Pariorites (supernatural beings) punish a bride and mother-in-law who were quarrelling at night. The experience made them never quarrel again, giving rise to the proverb «the young woman is beaten with a reed, the old woman with a cudgel».

content.value: Once a bride and her mother-in-law were quarrelling in the middle of the night when they heard a knock at the door. «Open up for us.» They asked who it was. «We are Pariorites, we go to the pariora. We are Pariorites, we go to the pariora.»

The old woman and the bride were very frightened and did not open the door. The Pariorites broke it down, entered, seized the bride first, and began to beat her with a stick, saying: «We are Pariorites, we go to the pariora.»
They then did the same to the old woman.
Before leaving, they said to them: «Next time do not quarrel, for woe to you.» From that day on, the mother-in-law and the bride never quarrelled again.
Author’s note: There is a variant of this account from which arose the proverb: «the young woman is beaten with a reed, the old woman with a cudgel.»

articles.title: The Voices in the Koudounotrypes – Ioannina
articles.author: G. K. Kavvadias
articles.excerpt: Tradition about koudounotrypes in the mountains of Ioannina: funnel-shaped holes from which the voices of the Sarakatsanaioi are heard. A warning to avoid any contact with them.

content.value: Walking in the mountains, shepherds come across deep holes that cut far into the earth, funnel-shaped. These are the «koudounotrypes». These holes seem to have no bottom. Indeed, no one had the courage or the means to explore them to their depths.

When you pass near them you hear strange sounds from within — loud moans, cries. These are the «Sarakatsanaioi» who are nestled in their bowels, making noise and shouting. If you do not wish to tangle with them, keep well away.

articles.title: The Ghosts of Prangi
articles.author: Christos Giannapoulos
articles.excerpt: Traditions about ghosts in Prangi, Evros: haunted houses, roads and natural spaces, methods of protection (stones) and the fear of the «evil hour».

content.value: In the evenings ghosts come out and children are very frightened. In desolate houses people imagine that spirits dwell — people who once lived there. If many children find themselves near a desolate house at night, they throw stones to drive away the ghosts. Even adults are haunted by this idea and hesitate to visit such places during the late night hours so as not to be present at the «evil hour» there.
So there are haunted houses, haunted roads (in the deep lane, for example, there appears a slain woman), haunted trees, rivers, ravines, wells, and so on.

articles.title: The Ghosts of Prangio
articles.author: P. Doulos
articles.excerpt: Personal account of a nocturnal encounter with a ghost in Prangio and the transformation of a spirit.

content.value: «Many have much to tell about ghosts. One night I was outside,» recounts a hearty old man. «The hour passed and I got up to leave.»

«When I went outside, a great fear gripped me. It was the hour when the ghosts came out. It was midnight. When I reached the square I stopped. At the well above, a ghost was appearing. I started to pray, then stopped. I was afraid.»

«I thought of turning back, but where would I go? Other roads had wells too. Should I go through the cemetery? Fear gripped me again. One moment I thought of going forward, the next of turning back, but I could not decide. I was drenched in cold sweat.»

«Finally I started forward, slowly. My eyes were fixed on the well. Nothing appeared. As I was about to pass, I said to myself: “It will eat me, it will eat me.” “I will close my eyes, I will run, and whatever happens.” When I finally passed the well and reached near the house, I looked behind me but there was nothing there. “It didn’t see me,” I said, and I was saved. I never again found myself outside at night.»

«And who has not chanced to see a ghost? A little above the square, in some ruins, there appears a cow being milked by a young woman. Many children have also seen it. Before, a bear would come out. It seems the spirit has changed form.»

articles.title: The Toulousoumi of Savra, Evros
articles.author: Nikolaos Karellas
articles.excerpt: Traditional practices for keeping vigil over the dead and protection from the Toulousoumi (ghost) in Savra, Evros.

content.value: Vigil over the dead. «Just as soldiers kept watch over Christ on the night, so we keep the night vigil over the dead, who are covered with a shroud up to the waist.»
«We take care that no cat passes over him, for if one does, the dead person turns into a phantom — a toulousoumi (ghost). If the deceased is very young, his family weeps for him a little.»
«The door and windows are kept open until he is buried.»

articles.title: Ritual of Contact with the Dead – Savra, Evros
articles.author: Nikolaos Karellas
articles.excerpt: Traditional ritual for communicating with deceased relatives using a mirror and a well on the eve of the Feast of the Ascension in Savra.

content.value: On the evening before the Feast of the Ascension, those who have deceased relatives and wish to see them go to a well and cover it with a red cloth.

In the morning at daybreak (of the Ascension), they take a large mirror and go to the covered well. They uncover it, wrap themselves in the red cloth, place the mirror at an angle over the mouth of the well, look toward the well and toward the mirror, and each one calls the name of their deceased and sees them in the mirror.

articles.title: The Ghosts of Didymoticho
articles.author: A. Tsakiri
articles.excerpt: Traditional beliefs about the origin of ghosts and ritual practices for interacting with them in Didymoticho.

content.value: They believed that the ghost had a brother named Bouboulas. Bouboulas was strong. His brother was jealous of him and asked a witch to tell him where his brother’s strength lay.
The witch told him that his brother’s strength lay in his right ankle. One day while Bouboulas was sleeping next to his brother, the brother went to kill him.
They struggled and Bouboulas won, remaining alone as the strong one that he was. Since then the other appears as a ghost.
The elders believed that ghosts, if they saw a man setting out at midnight, would appear before him.
Some men took a bread loaf (a ring-shaped loaf) in their hand and summoned the ghost. Men summoned the ghost in order to unite a female with a male and vice versa.
Also, if someone stayed outside past midnight, the ghosts would trail them.
Then those men, from outside their houses, would call to their wives to burn incense so that the ghosts would leave and not enter.

articles.title: The Ghost of the Vineyard – Didymoticho
articles.author: A. Tsakiri
articles.excerpt: Story about a ghost that appeared at a dry spring near a vineyard and terrified the residents of Didymoticho.

content.value: In the old days, a family had a vineyard. Near the vineyard there was a dry spring.
The family had a fifteen-year-old boy who would go to town with his donkey to fetch bread. That donkey would always go to the dry spring and put its snout inside.
The boy would beat the donkey, prod it to move forward — it would not budge. From the spring came a ghost, a child wrapped in swaddling clothes, which rolled and went to the feet of the donkey.
At the edge of the vineyard there was a small stream. The boy was very frightened. He said to his father: «Father, I will not go past our vineyard again.»
Then the father took the donkey and went himself. He reached the spring. The donkey behaved the same way. The ghost appeared; the father saw it, was terrified, and never returned to the vineyard.

articles.title: The Howling Ghost – Isaakio
articles.excerpt: Personal testimony about traditions of ghosts and supernatural phenomena in Isaakio, Evros.

content.value: One evening I happened to be in the upper quarter (the road that leads down to the vineyards) over on that side. I had heard various stories that at the spot where the strong wind blows, the voice of the Vlach is heard.

That voice, teacher, I myself heard with my own ears on that evening. He was crying out various words but I could not make out what he was saying. They say of this voice that in the old days (who knows when), a Vlach was slaughtered so that his gold coins could be taken, and ever since then each year he cries out for people to hear him. It was this time of year that the poor man was slaughtered.
This voice was not heard by me alone but by many others from the village as well, teacher.

And that zouzulo again, which got tangled around our feet — that too was something else again. It appeared to me one evening on the road. How frightened I was I cannot tell you. You, teacher, may not believe these things, but I saw them with my own eyes and heard them with my own ears.
And the bell that was heard ringing from that little estate there — I heard that too.
